after: The third record line is Dana's record. Its id `mem-EXAMPLE4-0000-4000-8000-0000example4` is the id of the proposal.
Its namespace is now `/project/example-project/shared/`. Its text did not change.
`actorId` still says `dana`: the author. `approvedBy` says `alice`, and `approvedAt` says when.
Every member of `example-project` can now recall it: Alice, Bruno, Chen and Dana.

steps.title: The proposals namespace is empty
before: The move took the record out of Dana's proposals namespace. Dana lists the namespace a few minutes after the approve.

frame.title: dana@laptop: ~/example-project
frame.source: the AWS CLI help of `list-memory-records`, and the empty answer of the live proof on an own empty namespace (round 1); right after the approve, the live list still showed the record (round 2)

after: A record has exactly one namespace. Approve made no copy.
Right after the approve, the list can still show the record for a few minutes. The record itself is already in the shared namespace: the recall of step 2 finds it there.

learned: An approved record keeps its id and its text.
Its metadata names the author, the maintainer and the time of the approve.
From now on, every member of the project recalls it.
cannot: A record cannot be in the proposals namespace and in the shared namespace at the same time.
A person outside `example-project` cannot recall it. IAM denies that person a read of `/project/example-project/shared/`.
The approved record cannot carry a metadata key that Dana added herself. The core copies only the keys of propose.
notVerified: The empty list of step 3 after the index caught up.
